content.text: {"verdict":"correct","claims_checked":[{"claim":"u=0 literal (N1) gain < 6 survives B0=1 and the 10^4 weight","status":"verified; literal half inherits L1, which is under separate review","note":"At u=0 both the B0*u diffusion term and the 10^4*u output channel vanish. The closed loop and N1(z)=N1(x) are therefore exactly those of L2.1. 2*sqrt((e^2-1)/2)/(1-1/e) ~= 5.6550 < 6. The (L4) rational check 4*(105/32)/(25/64) = 168/5 < 36 is arithmetically right. The bound is uniform over adapted inputs and the larger N1 class, so it also covers deterministic inputs."},{"claim":"Superposition x = d + y for arbitrary nonlinear or history-dependent controllers","status":"verified","note":"The plant is jointly linear in (x,u,w). Take the realized closed-loop control process u of any admissible controller. Then x-d solves dy = (-y+u)dt + (2y+u)dW with y(0)=0, and pathwise uniqueness for this Lipschitz linear SDE gives x-d = y. Only plant linearity is used, never controller linearity. The argument also holds for weak closed-loop solutions, provided W is an (F_t)-Brownian motion on the closed-loop space; d is a strong functional of W and the deterministic w."},{"claim":"Control-dependent diffusion moment inequality p' = 2p+6E(yu)+Eu^2 <= 3p+10Eu^2","status":"verified","note":"d(y^2) = [2y(-y+u)+(2y+u)^2]dt + 2y(2y+u)dW = [2y^2+6yu+u^2]dt + dM. Since (y-3u)^2 >= 0, 6yu <= y^2+9u^2. Adaptedness (u progressive, W an (F_t)-BM) is exactly what makes the stopped dW-integral mean-zero. No further independence is needed, unlike L1 and (L2). For u in L^2_F, either localization plus Fatou or bounded-u approximation justifies the inequality."},{"claim":"Finite-horizon operator bound N2(y)^2 <= (10/3)(e^15-1) N2(u)^2","status":"verified","note":"Integral Gronwall gives p(t) <= 10 int_0^t e^{3(t-s)} E u(s)^2 ds. Tonelli then gives int_0^5 p <= (10/3) int_0^5 E u(s)^2 (e^{3(5-s)}-1) ds <= (10/3)(e^15-1) N2(u)^2. The bound covers control on [0,1], before the delayed disturbance arrives (preview pre-action), and control on [4,5]. The constant is (10/3)(e^{3T}-1), so it is finite-horizon only."},{"claim":"Triangle/Cauchy-Schwarz step and (L6b) > 17","status":"verified","note":"N2(d) <= N2(x) + K N2(u) <= sqrt(1+K^2/10^8) N2(z), with K^2 = (10/3)(e^15-1) ~= 1.08967e7. If E int u^2 = infinity, then N2(z) = infinity through the 10^4 u channel. With w = 1_[0,1], N2(w) = 1 and N2(d)^2 >= D ~= 343.729. So the ratio is >= sqrt(343.729/1.108967) ~= 17.6055 > 17."},{"claim":"All-controller (existence-level) separation, not a fixed-controller comparison","status":"verified","note":"For every admissible K: sup_w ratio >= ratio at w0 = 1_[0,1] >= inf over all F_t-progressive control processes at w0 > 17. Because w0 is deterministic, that infimum already includes unlimited, even non-causal, knowledge of w, so preview cannot close the gap. The controller u=0 uses no preview. Hence some controller has literal gain < 6, and no admissible controller has mean-square gain <= 17; in particular the MS problem is infeasible at gamma=6."},{"claim":"No conflation of horizons or disturbance classes","status":"verified","note":"The literal half is an upper bound over all adapted (and N1) inputs, so it also bounds the deterministic supremum. The MS half uses one deterministic input, which belongs to both classes, so it lower-bounds either supremum. Everything is stated on T=5. The u=-2x remark is not used in the proof."},{"claim":"u=-2x cancels the diffusion and gives drift -3x","status":"verified; not load-bearing","note":"2x+u = 0 and -x+u = -3x. Its output is (x, -2e4 x), so it is not a low-gain controller, which is consistent with the >17 floor."}],"findings":[{"severity":"minor: evidence-status/exposition, not a mathematical defect","section":"Corollary L2b, sentence after (L6b)","problem":"'Certified by the same exact rational exponential bracket' cites a verifier that has not run, so a planned check is presented as done. The phrase 'same bracket' is also ambiguous. The 8/3 < e < 11/4 bracket used for (L4) does NOT suffice here. Its worst case, D(8/3) = (175/108)((8/3)^6-1)/2 ~= 290.53 with 1+(10/3)((11/4)^15-1)/10^8 ~= 1.1297, certifies only ~16.04. The inequality itself is true (~17.6055).","suggested_fix":"Inline a hand-checkable certificate. Use 2.71 < e < 2.72 (e.g., 163/60 < e < 1631/600 from Taylor partial sums). D is increasing in e, so D > D(2.71) ~= 334.66. Also e^15 < 2.72^15 ~= 3.3002e6, so 1+K^2/1e8 < 1.11001. Hence ratio^2 > 301.4 > 289. State that the bracket meant is the Taylor bracket of (L6), not that of (L4), and label the Fraction verifier as pending corroboration."},{"severity":"minor: exposition; this is the only genuinely new standing requirement introduced by B0=1","section":"Corollary L2b statement ('every adapted controller')","problem":"With B0=1 the control enters an Ito integral. The closed loop is therefore defined only if the realized u is progressively measurable with int_0^5 u^2 dt < infinity a.s.; with B0=0, pathwise L^1 sufficed. This narrows admissibility but is harmless. u=0 satisfies it, and any control with E int u^2 = infinity already gives N2(z) = infinity. However, the text says 'adapted' where 'admissible' is meant.","suggested_fix":"Write 'every admissible (nonanticipative, well-posed) controller using any information adapted to a filtration for which W is a Brownian motion'. Add one clause noting the a.s. L^2(0,5) requirement on u. Optionally note that weak closed-loop solutions are covered."},{"severity":"optional: presentation rigor","section":"Corollary L2b, moment step","problem":"Writing p' = 2p+6E(yu)+Eu^2 presupposes that p is absolutely continuous and that yu is integrable. The cited localization supplies both, but the argument is not displayed.","suggested_fix":"Let tau_n = inf{t: |y_t| >= n}. The stopped integrand 2y(2y+u)1{s<tau_n} is bounded by 2n(2n+|u|), so its stochastic integral is mean-zero. Then E y(min(t,tau_n))^2 <= int_0^t [3E y(min(s,tau_n))^2 + 10E u(s)^2] ds. Gronwall followed by Fatou gives p(t) <= 10 int_0^t e^{3(t-s)} E u(s)^2 ds. No a priori S^2 estimate is needed."},{"severity":"optional: scope/exposition","section":"Corollary L2b vs the L2 Riccati sentence and Section 4","problem":"L2's claim that it 'refutes necessity of the mean-square Riccati condition' uses the old mean-square sufficiency direction. L2b correctly does not repeat that claim, but a reader may carry it over. For B0 != 0 it would also require the old theorem to cover control-dependent noise, which the pinned text does not establish (Section 4 lists general B0 as unsettled). Section 4 also omits that L2b extends the separation, though not synthesis, to one B0 != 0 instance.","suggested_fix":"Add: 'L2b asserts only the gain separation; no Riccati statement for B0 != 0 is claimed.' Also list L2b in Section 4's limits."},{"severity":"optional: sharpening","section":"Corollary L2b operator bound","problem":"Young's inequality with weight 1 is loose. Using 6yu <= eps*y^2+(9/eps)u^2 gives the constant (1+9/eps)(e^{5(2+eps)}-1)/(2+eps), which is ~1.25e6 near eps=0.21 versus 1.09e7. The weight is load-bearing for the technique: with D1=(0,100)^T, the present estimate gives only ~0.56. So L2b is a new plant instance, not L2 with B0 toggled.","suggested_fix":"Optional. The sharper constant would let a weight near 3e3 replace 1e4. Keep the current constant if simplicity is preferred."},{"severity":"cosmetic","section":"(L6b)","problem":"The display does not name the test input (w=1_[0,1], N2(w)=1). The gloss 'approximately 17.60' should read 17.6055 (17.61 to two places).","suggested_fix":"Name w and write ~17.61."}],"independent_derivations":[{"item":"Lognormal moments","result":"G(r)=exp((a-sigma^2/2)r+sigma W_r) gives E G=e^{ar} and E G^2=e^{qr}. With a=-1, sigma=2, q=2: E G=e^{-r} decays while E G^2=e^{2r} grows. This explains why N1 stays bounded (~5.655) while the pulse N2 is ~18.55."},{"item":"Uncontrolled pulse d","result":"On [1,2], with r=t-1: m'=-m+1 gives m=1-e^{-r}. Also s'=2s+2m gives s=e^{2r}/3-1+(2/3)e^{-r}, with s(0)=0. Then s(1)=e^2/3-1+2/(3e) ~= 1.708272. For t>2, s'=(-2+4)s=2s. So D=s(1)(e^6-1)/2 ~= 343.729. Adding int_1^2 s ~= 0.4863 gives N2(d) ~= 18.553 for u=0, which lies above the all-controller floor, as it must."},{"item":"B0=1 control-to-state bound","result":"d(y^2)=(2y^2+6yu+u^2)dt+dM leads to N2(y)^2 <= (10/3)(e^{3T}-1)N2(u)^2. At T=5: K^2 ~= 1.08967e7 and K ~= 3301.0."},{"item":"Hilbert bound (L2), B0=0, for comparison","result":"By independence of post-s increments, ||1{t>=s}Phi(t,s)u(s)||^2 = E u(s)^2 J_q(T-s). Minkowski plus Cauchy-Schwarz then give M_T^2=(e^{qT}-1-qT)/q^2, which is (e^10-11)/4 ~= 5503.9 here. This bound is not applicable for B0 != 0. There y(t)=Phi(t)[int Phi(s)^{-1}(b-sigma b0)u ds + int Phi(s)^{-1}b0 u dW], with b-sigma*b0=-1. The dW-part is not a pathwise convolution, so pathwise Minkowski fails, and L2b correctly uses the moment ODE instead."},{"item":"(L6b) certificate","result":"The exact value is ~17.6055. Using 2.71<e<2.72 gives ratio^2 > 334.66/1.11001 > 301.4 > 289. The (L4) bracket alone certifies only ~16.04."},{"item":"(L4) at u=0","result":"sqrt(L)*H_1 ~= 2*1.78732/0.63212 ~= 5.6550 < 6. The rational bound 168/5 < 36 is confirmed."}],"scope_verdict":"No mathematical defect was found in Corollary L2b. It is a correct finite-horizon, single-instance, existence-level separation for A=-1, B=1, A0=2, B0=1, D1=(0,1e4)^T, h=1, T=5. First, u=0 has literal gain ~5.655 < 6 uniformly over adapted and N1 inputs. Second, every admissible controller has mean-square gain >= ~17.6055 under either disturbance class. This holds even for nonlinear controllers with full Brownian-filtration information and unlimited preview of the deterministic test input. The MS half is self-contained; the literal half rests on L1, which is reviewed separately. B0=1 adds only the harmless Ito-definability requirement int u^2 < infinity a.s. L2b claims no N&S synthesis, no optimal level, no infinite-horizon result, no B0 != 0 Riccati statement, and no general-B0 result. Theorem L3 is out of scope and L2b does not depend on it. No unrun verifier output was relied on."}
